title: Marcellus Shale Mineral Rights
metaTitle: Sell Marcellus Shale Mineral Rights in West Virginia
metaDescription: West Virginia Marcellus owners in Doddridge, Harrison, Marshall, Wetzel and Tyler counties: get your abstract reviewed and a benchmarked offer before you sign anything.
heroLead: Every Marcellus tract in West Virginia carries a paper trail, and the value of your interest is usually written into that trail before a single royalty check confirms it.
intro: The Marcellus in West Virginia runs through the north-central counties in a band that includes Doddridge, Harrison, Marshall, Wetzel, Tyler, Ritchie and parts of Monongalia and Marion. Horizontal development took off there around 2008 and 2009, but most of the mineral estates underneath those laterals were severed decades earlier, often through coal or timber company deeds from the early 1900s that carved the surface away from the oil, gas and coal beneath it.

That gap between the drilling date and the severance date is where most title problems live. Before we quote anything on a Marcellus interest, we pull the deed and lease chain at the county clerk's office and compare it against whatever operator division order paperwork you're holding. A number without a title check behind it is a guess, not an offer.

sections.heading: Where the play sits and what it means for your tract
paragraphs: The Marcellus in this part of West Virginia sits roughly 4,000 to 8,500 feet down, thickening toward the Pennsylvania line and thinning as you move south and west out of the core counties. Laterals run one to two miles, and a single well now typically drains a unit assembled from dozens of separate tracts, which means your royalty decimal is often a small slice of a large pooled unit rather than a clean fraction of your original acreage.

Operators active in the West Virginia Marcellus have shifted over the years, with EQT, Antero Resources, Northeast Natural Energy and Southwestern's successor entities holding the bulk of current production. Older leases from the 2008-2011 land rush were frequently assigned two or three times before a well was ever permitted, so the party paying your royalty today is rarely the party whose landman knocked on the door.

sections.heading: Legacy vertical wells layered under the horizontal program
paragraphs: A lot of West Virginia Marcellus tracts already had shallow vertical wells producing out of the Big Injun, Gordon or Fifth Sand before the horizontal boom arrived. Those older leases sometimes cover only the shallow rights, or they cover 'oil and gas' broadly and got swept into the deeper Marcellus unit by their own habendum clause. Sorting out whether your shallow lease actually reaches the Marcellus, or whether a separate deep-rights lease was signed later, changes what you own and what a buyer will pay for it.

We see this most often on tracts where a family kept a small stripper well running for personal use or minimal royalty for thirty years, then discovered the same acreage sat inside a new horizontal unit with a different operator and a different decimal entirely.

sections.heading: Flat-rate leases and the conversion that changed West Virginia royalties
paragraphs: West Virginia has more surviving flat-rate leases than almost any other Appalachian state, agreements written before the 1982 statutory minimum that paid a flat annual sum, sometimes a few hundred dollars, instead of a percentage of production. State law has since pushed those leases toward a minimum one-eighth royalty on gas actually produced, and the 2018 amendments extended that treatment to horizontal Marcellus wells specifically. If your family's lease predates that fix and nobody ever filed the paperwork to convert it, you may be owed more than the operator is currently paying, and that unresolved conversion issue also affects what your interest is worth to a buyer.

We check the recorded lease date and royalty clause against the conversion statute before we value a flat-rate tract, because an unconverted flat-rate lease and a properly converted one are not the same asset even if the acreage is identical.

sections.heading: Heirship and fractional interests inside Marcellus units
paragraphs: Because so much West Virginia mineral ownership passed down through generations without formal probate, a single Marcellus royalty check is often split among a dozen or more heirs holding fractional undivided interests, some as small as a few hundredths of one percent. The state's Co-Tenancy Modernization and Majority Protection Act lets a majority of the identified owners lease or participate on behalf of unlocated or nonconsenting co-tenants for horizontal units, but it doesn't fix the underlying title. If your name only shows up because a great-aunt died intestate in 1974 and nobody ever recorded a settlement, that gap in the chain has to be documented, not guessed at, before a sale can close cleanly.

faqs.question: How is a West Virginia Marcellus royalty different from a flat vertical well royalty?
faqs.answer: A horizontal Marcellus unit typically pools many tracts, so your royalty decimal reflects your acreage's share of the whole unit rather than the well sitting on your land specifically. Two neighboring owners can have very different decimals depending on when they signed and how the unit was drawn.

faqs.question: What if my family's lease is one of the old flat-rate agreements?
faqs.answer: We pull the recorded lease and check the royalty clause against West Virginia's conversion statute. Depending on the lease date and whether the well is horizontal, you may be entitled to the statutory minimum royalty going forward, which we factor into any offer we make.

faqs.question: Do I need to sort out heirship before I can sell?
faqs.answer: Not always before we make an offer, but it has to be resolved before closing. We can often work from the recorded probate or intestate succession records at the county clerk's office and tell you early what documentation the closing will require.

faqs.question: Can you tell me what my Marcellus interest is worth without seeing my lease?
faqs.answer: Not accurately. Values vary with the unit's decimal, the operator's current activity, recent royalty statements and whether the lease is flat-rate or percentage. We ask for a copy of your last division order or royalty check to start a real conversation.

faqs.question: Why does the operator on my check keep changing?
faqs.answer: Marcellus leasehold in West Virginia has been assigned and sold repeatedly since the original land rush. The operating company can change without any change to your underlying lease terms, though it's worth confirming the assignment was properly recorded at the courthouse.
